messages:
Sam AE: Quick Q from Acme POC — their security team is asking for explicit breach notification timing and scope for the POC. They want a 72h initial notification commitment and to know who the customer-facing IR contact is. cc @Chris SE
Chris SE: Short answer: we can acknowledge and provide initial findings within 72h for hosted POCs. For VPC/on‑prem POCs we provide the technical findings and recommended notices, but the customer typically handles external communications unless we have a paid IR engagement. @Legal (Maya) can confirm legal wording.
Legal (Maya): Correct. Hosted: Redwood will notify affected customers per contract and provide timeline updates. VPC/on‑prem: we deliver findings and recommended notice language; customer owns public notification unless contract says otherwise. Note: standard free trial/POC SOWs do NOT include forensic engagements — that requires an addendum/SOW and often an NDA.
Oliver Security: Operational notes: we can deliver initial triage artifacts (logs, event timeline, impacted resources) within 48–72h for hosted POCs. Full forensics or deep-dive requires formal engagement. Severity guide: Critical = confirmed data exfil / live key exposure; High = authenticated compromise of non‑PII services; Medium/Low = isolated failures or no evidence of compromise.
Sam AE: Got it. Procurement specifically asked for a sample 72h notice they can show their legal. Can someone drop a short template we can share?
Oliver Security: Sample 72h notice (drop to customer):
```
Within 72 hours Redwood will:
1) Acknowledge receipt of incident report and point of contact.
2) Provide an initial incident summary and list of potentially impacted resources.
3) Share immediate mitigations taken and recommended next steps.
4) Provide contact for follow-up: ir@redwood.com.
For hosted deployments Redwood will coordinate customer notifications per contract. For VPC/on‑prem, Redwood will supply findings and notice language; customer will manage public communications unless otherwise agreed.
```
Chris SE: + :thumbsup: — also flag that keys and customer data access require escalation to Security Ops immediately.
Jenny PM: Reminder — POC contract matters. The free POC template explicitly disclaims SLAs. If they need contractual 72h commitments we need a POC-for-enterprise addendum (paid). Sales, confirm whether Acme is willing to accept an addendum.
Sam AE: I'll confirm with Acme procurement today and ask if they'll sign the addendum. If they want us to own notifications for VPC we should ticket Legal for pricing and Maya for redline.
Legal (Maya): I'll draft a short addendum and a redline for the POC SOW that includes notification obligations and the limits of forensic scope. Posting a draft by EOD. @Oliver Security — I'll lean on you for the technical wording.
Anya CISO: Quick note for procurement: include contact handoff template with at least two IR contacts and a high‑level escalation matrix (S1/S2/S3) so customers can show their execs how incidents will be handled.
Sam AE: Perfect, thanks everyone. I'll update Acme after Maya posts the draft.
